children: Australian government spending edged higher in the second quarter, data showed on Tuesday, providing just a small lift to growth in an otherwise slowing economy.
Spending on operational items rose 0.6% in the June quarter from the previous quarter to an inflation-adjusted A$159.7 billion ($114.49 billion), the Australian Bureau of Statistics reported.

Total investment in fixed assets by the government and public enterprises fell 1.3% after a run of strong outcomes, to A$38.2 billion. In all, the ABS estimated total public spending added 0.1 percentage points to second-quarter gross domestic product.
